newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Faulding sees FDA approval for herpes drug.
newsitem.headline: Faulding sees FDA approval for herpes drug.

text.p: Pharmaceutical firm F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said on Monday that its United States operations had received tentative approval to market its acyclovir injection, pending expiration this month of the original patent.

In a statement, Faulding's U.S. subsidiary Faulding Inc said the product was the generic version of Zovirax, Glaxo Wellcome's brand of acyclovir sodium sterile powder which in 1996 had sales of about US$74 million.
Final approval by the Food and Drug Adminstration (FDA) was expected on the expiration of the brand's patent on April 22, the company said.
Faulding Inc said acyclovir was an antiviral drug active against herpes viruses.
Faulding's product was a sterile solution which did not require reconstitution with sterile water, unlike the brand product Zovirax, it said.
Faulding said the injection, to be manufactured at its injectable facility in Musgrave, Victoria, was the fifth FDA approval received by the U.S. subsidiary this calendar year.
